clue.text: Dancing better slim lass — one of her pupils?

definitions.text: Dancing better slim lass — one of her pupils?

indicators.note: the letters of the three words that follow are set dancing, jigging into a new order

explanation.surface: A slender girl dances well, and the clue wonders whether she trains under a particular teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dancing' rearranges BETTER SLIM LASS; read whole, the clue also describes the answer, whose pupil the dancing lass might be.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballet company's dance teacher and rehearsal director trains the dancers, so a graceful girl dancing well could be among her pupils.

clue.text: Source of berries found on walk in the countryside?

definitions.text: Source of berries found on walk in the countryside?

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it begins, so its opening letter is taken

parts.note: a ramble is a leisurely country walk

explanation.surface: A hedgerow plant laden with fruit spotted while out hiking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Source of' gives the first letter of 'berries', B, and a country walk is a RAMBLE; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The blackberry bush grows wild in hedgerows and yields fruit that walkers pick in late summer.

clue.text: Unremitting in support of party in need of a large workforce

definitions.text: in need of a large workforce

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporting word sits beneath the other, so this one goes below the party

parts.note: Labour is a major British political party
unremitting effort is intensive, concentrated and relentless

explanation.surface: A relentless political backer of a party that needs many hands.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'in support of' puts INTENSIVE underneath LABOUR, the British party.
explanation.definitionFit: An industry or task requiring much human effort compared with machinery or capital needs many workers.

clue.text: Food kept in meat safe

indicators.note: the answer is kept inside the run of letters across the two following words

explanation.surface: Provisions stored in an old-fashioned meat safe, a ventilated cupboard for keeping meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, grub or things to eat; a café sign promising snacks uses this slang word.

clue.text: Mouthful from TV detective ending in 'hell'!

parts.note: Inspector Morse is the Oxford detective of the long-running ITV series

indicators.note: the ending of the word that follows supplies its final letter

explanation.surface: An exclamation from a television detective whose catchphrase ends with a curse.
explanation.walkthrough: Inspector Morse is a famous British TV detective in Oxford; 'ending in' takes the last letter of 'hell'.
explanation.definitionFit: A small bite or bit of food, enough to fill the mouth once.

clue.text: Daughter unfortunately knocked over pub's self-service food station

indicators.note: something knocked over is upended, so in a down answer these letters run backwards

parts.note: alas is an exclamation meaning unfortunately
a bar is a pub, and the possessive is just surface

explanation.surface: A clumsy daughter has sadly toppled the pub's buffet counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked over' turns the first two pieces round, making SALAD; 'unfortunately' looks like an anagram signal but gives a word.
explanation.definitionFit: A counter of cold vegetables and dressings where diners help themselves, found in restaurants and pubs.

clue.text: Learn in set playing a racket sport

indicators.note: the letters are playing about, so they are mixed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Pick up a game by taking part in a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' scrambles LEARN IN SET.
explanation.definitionFit: The original indoor court game from which lawn tennis developed, played with rackets in walled courts like Hampton Court's.

clue.text: Point of view where Plato perhaps studied philosophy?

definitions.meaning: a particular outlook or set of beliefs held by a group
read literally, an academy devoted to reflection, like the one where the Greek thinker learned

explanation.definitionFit: A body of opinion shared by thinkers, and taken literally an educational institution devoted to thinking.

clue.text: Careful with money, French girl pressing uniform

indicators.note: the girl presses up against the letter before her, so the two sit side by side

parts.note: U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet
gal is an informal word for girl

explanation.surface: A thrifty French girl irons her school uniform herself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pressing' looks like ironing but only means the girl sits right against the uniform letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrifty and sparing, unwilling to spend more than needed.

clue.text: A nip swallowed by bishop and judge

indicators.note: the bishop's letters take the nip inside them, as if swallowing it

parts.note: RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop
a nip is a small bite

explanation.surface: A bishop gulps down a drink, then a judge appears too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nip' looks like a tot of spirits but is BITE; RR (Right Reverend) is a bishop's title.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who decides a dispute is a referee or adjudicator.

clue.text: Cordelia's father protecting the kid, perhaps

indicators.note: the father wraps around the next word, sheltering it inside

parts.note: King Lear is the father of Cordelia in Shakespeare's tragedy

explanation.surface: King Lear shields a child, perhaps his youngest daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kid' looks like a child but is the soft goatskin; 'protecting' signals an enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: Kid is a soft material made from young goatskin, one example of tanned hide.

clue.text: Bowled, dismissed in match

parts.note: B is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for bowled
a dismissed batter is out

explanation.surface: A cricketer bowled and sent off during a game.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, 'bowled' is a way of being dismissed, abbreviated B on scorecards.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxing or wrestling contest is a fight or bout of competition.

clue.text: Stubborn chief, resilient

parts.note: a head is a chief or leader
resilient means tough, strong

explanation.surface: A boss who is obstinate and tough.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilful and determined to have one's own way, obstinate.

clue.text: Able-bodied boys in blue serve adequately

parts.note: fit means healthy and able-bodied
the Bill is British slang for the police, who wear blue uniforms

explanation.surface: Healthy police officers do a good enough job.
explanation.walkthrough: THE BILL is British slang for the police, also a long-running TV police drama.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning to be suitable or do what is required.

clue.text: Find out what's legal after start of embargo?

indicators.note: the legal word follows after that opening letter
the start of the word that follows is its opening letter

parts.note: licit means lawful, legal

explanation.surface: Discover which trade is still permitted once a ban begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start of' takes E from 'embargo'; LICIT comes after it.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw out information or a response from someone, discovering it by questioning.

clue.text: Bird flying low by a port

indicators.note: by means beside, placing one piece next to the other

parts.note: tawny is a type of port wine, aged in wood

indicators.note: letters flying about are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A bird skims low beside a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like a harbour but is the wine, TAWNY; 'flying' shuffles LOW.
explanation.definitionFit: A common brown woodland owl of Europe, known for its hooting call.

clue.text: Bird, bright orange duck

parts.note: flaming describes a fiery, vivid colour
a duck is zero in cricket, written O

explanation.surface: A vivid orange waterfowl.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a score of zero in cricket, so O.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall pink wading bird with long legs and a hooked beak.

clue.text: Restructuring of NATO unlikely, so don't mention it

indicators.note: restructuring rebuilds the alliance's letters in a different order

parts.note: a tall story is an unlikely one

explanation.surface: Reforming the military alliance is improbable, so best not to raise it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Restructuring of' rearranges NATO into NOTA; TALL as in a tall tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A polite reply to thanks, meaning it was no trouble whatever.

clue.text: Unknown to knight, famous physicist

parts.note: something unknown to you is new to you
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A knight unaware of a celebrated scientist.
explanation.walkthrough: N is the knight in chess notation; the physicist was himself knighted.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Isaac, the English scientist who formulated the laws of motion and gravitation.

clue.text: Weapon carried by cop is tolerated

indicators.note: the letters are carried inside the words that follow, across the gaps

explanation.surface: A police officer is allowed to bear a firearm.
explanation.definitionFit: A handgun, a small firearm held in one hand.

clue.text: Confused monarch about British seafood

indicators.note: the confused word goes about the British letter, enclosing it

parts.note: someone confused is lost
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the late Queen

explanation.surface: A bewildered king surrounded by British fish dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confused' looks like an anagram signal but gives a synonym; 'about' signals an enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: A large marine crustacean with claws, eaten as a delicacy.

clue.text: Stiffly formal journalist put in the picture

parts.note: prim means stiffly proper and formal
ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A starchy reporter has been briefed.
explanation.definitionFit: Briefed or prepared in advance, given the necessary information.

clue.text: We remind comic about one of Oscar's ladies?

indicators.note: comic means funny or absurd, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A request to remind a comedian about a woman Oscar Wilde wrote about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comic' rearranges WE REMIND; RE means about. Oscar is Oscar Wilde, author of Lady Windermere's Fan.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady Windermere is the title character of Oscar Wilde's comedy, one of the playwright's heroines.

clue.text: Thoroughly search company doctor

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A firm's medic looks everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: To go through methodically, as with a fine-toothed instrument through hair.

clue.text: A short cut in neighbourhood

indicators.note: short means cut off at the end, so the final letter goes

parts.note: to reap is to cut a crop

explanation.surface: A quick route through the local streets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short cut' looks like a quick route; 'short' trims the last letter of REAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A district or locality, a part of a town.

clue.text: Popular one in work on view

indicators.note: the first two pieces go in the middle of the others

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work, followed by ON as written
in means fashionable, popular
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A fashionable person in a job that is on display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals that the popular one goes inside the work on, splitting that phrase; 'view' is the definition, not part of 'on view'.
explanation.definitionFit: A belief or judgement held about something, one's take on it.

clue.text: The perfect male Republican — Reagan, initially, when put in power

indicators.note: the two letters are put into the word for power

parts.note: might means power or strength

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of the following name

explanation.surface: An ideal man is a Republican, and Reagan when elected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes R from Reagan; 'put in' places R + R inside MIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: The ideal partner or husband, the one man destined to suit someone.

clue.text: Consider commendable, fine player's sense of well-being

parts.note: to feel is to consider or believe
good means praiseworthy
F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine
a player is an actor; the possessive is surface

explanation.surface: Rating a good actor highly gives a sense of contentment.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase for the general optimism and contentment felt by people, especially about the economy.
